steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: How tiny we seem when we stand beside the tracks of this ship.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, it's a most impressive war machine.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: With their bodies as barriers, the Nachzehrer halted its advance at a tremendous cost. The Banshee's shrieks, powerful enough to shatter consciousness, only managed to force the Leithanians to retreat below deck...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: If not for the Catastrophe and the rough terrain in this valley—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We're so far behind, and time is running out.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Kazdel must have equally powerful weapons, if not more so.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All our previous attempts have failed...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A century ago, few believed we could build a nomadic city out of Kazdel, yet we did. If we are to catch up to them now, we cannot afford to take the conventional path.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We have word from the Damazti. The battleships on the horizon are slowing down.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Have they given up?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, the Kurfürst's orders were to continue the pursuit, but the commander of the fleet ordered them to slow down.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They're concerned about the Catastrophes and the terrain. They've seen what happened to this ship.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: At the current rate, we can expect to engage them at dusk.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We have bought enough time for Kazdel to retreat.
Theresa looks back at the two storms entwining on the wastes, trying to catch a glimpse of the city.
She sees nothing. Where is Kazdel now? Is it still moving through the storm? Are the people in the shelters safe?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The storms are converging. Our retreat has been cut off. A battle is inevitable... Theresis?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I never thought I'd see you lose focus on the battlefield.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What's that?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's...
The storms rage, the young taunting the old.
The newborn storm slams into the dying storm to the war drums of thunder.
Roiling air currents clash and combine between the two storms...
Violence begets peace, and a passage appears where the storms converge.
Lightning flashes and thunder cracks.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: A path through the storm.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The storm...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Let's go, Theresa. The storm has given us a path.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Those who survive through it will have another chance.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We'll do it together.
The Damazti Cluster passes their command to every Sarkaz present.
The warriors see their leaders walk into the storm side by side and follow with no hesitation.
The procession advances into the tempest, the strong supporting the weak, the brave encouraging the fearful.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Do you see that, Theresis?
Within the roar of the tempest, they seem to hear the voice from the snowstorm in that childhood dream.
They see—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...The prophecy.
The thin, cloaked figure turns at the sound of her voice and sees the storm-bound procession.
Theresis sees a child. Mist, gilded by the setting sun, shrouds her shoulders, rising and blending with the shrieking winds above.
He takes off his gauntlet and stretches his bare hand into the mist.
The mist dissipates, and in his bloodied hand is the stone blade that the child is holding.
(Slurring) Yew... argh! Gra... grab!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What are you doing here?
(Slurring) Hom. Yew... hom! Hom!
(Slurring) Yew! Came in! Home!
The child wrestles the blade from Theresis's hand and points it again at Theresis and the procession behind him.
There is no difference between man and beast to the child who grew up in the wastes.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You want to kill me?
(Slurring) Keel... kill you!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Nobody taught her how to speak. She simply emulates the sounds made by those who pass by.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Theresis?
Theresis looks down silently at the thin figure.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Let me show you how to hold a knife.
(Slurring) You!
The child hesitates for a moment, before putting her knife in Theresis's outstretched hand.
(Slurring) ...Me. You! Bring, me... bring, me!
Theresis gazes into Theresa's eyes.
Prophecy.
'A sword to slay the regent king, a spear to pierce the royal ring.'
But they have never cared much for prophecy.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Come with me. The home of the Sarkaz is not on the barrens.
'Do you have a name?'
'Name? Me.'
'From now on, you have a new name.'
'Ascalon.'
Ten days later...
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Look, doctor! The furnace has been relit!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Is it moving? The city's finally moving? Ouch...

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Careful! Your wounds might open again...

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: I've got to go to the furnace. The furnace burns again, and Kazdel still sails...

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: The Leithanians didn't manage to kill us!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Oh, er, I didn't mean you, doctor.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Come with me to see it. You deserve the same honor as the warriors who survived.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: But... I'm not Sarkaz.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: You people are heroes, too.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Come watch Their Highnesses command the Goliath to support the leaning furnace! Watch the sparks fly when iron hammers beat upon the broken core!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Hear the elegy of the Banshee, and witness the final journey of fallen heroes when they enter the furnace to fuel it!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: This used to be an occasion that only the Sarkaz could see.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: I would love to go, but there are still a lot of wounded to treat.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Alright, tell you what, I'll bring back a couple bottles of booze and some fresh fruit, and we'll...

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: You're not allowed to drink! And who the heck drinks in a medic tent?

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Come on, it's just a little flesh wound.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: No means no! It's your Oripathy that's the problem! Not to mention you're a terrible drinker.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: When did you ever see me drink? Oh, that time when I was drunk and came to you with a bunch of Oripathy bombs.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Look, that was the only time in all these years. You know I can't afford booze.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: *sigh* I can't stop you... why don't you go yourself?

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Won't be the same without you.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: But... I'm a Leithanian...

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: And? Do you support those nobles who profit off war?

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: I ran away from home because I couldn't stand them!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: There you have it. Hm? Wait a second. You say you ran away from home? Were you noble—

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: I was kind of thinking, your equipment doesn't look like it's from Babel—

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: —Well, I won't speculate. It does nobody any good.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: So, you can go on your own.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: I doubt the soldiers on the front lines would get along with a Leithanian...

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: When I saw the Leithanians string my father up by a sewer entrance to humiliate him, I never imagined I could befriend a Caprinae doctor either.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Back then, the only people who showed us any kindness were poor, Infected, or both.

steps.name: Excited Sarkaz
steps.text: Right, enough of the sad stuff. Be back in a jiffy.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Seriously, since when did the Sarkaz become so glib-tongued with me?

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: I wonder if this count as progress, Theresa...

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: In any case, Kazdel is moving again. Things will get better.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Back already? Well, it's about time you laid down—

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Oh, sorry, I thought you were someone else.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Wait, your wounds are really bad... nobody treated your Arts burns?

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: The Leithanians did it. My son's dead. They burned him alive before my very eyes. I was the only one who lived.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: ...At least let me see your wounds.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: They burned him alive. He was screaming. They used Arts to hang him in the air, for everyone to see.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: My brothers are dead. My captain is dead. The Leithanians stood on the high ground, their raised staffs looked just like...
With bloodshot eyes, the nearly deranged Sarkaz fixates on the doctor's staff abandoned in the corner.
The emblem of the home she had left behind hangs from the staff.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Like a real...
The doctor does not sense the hostility.
She lifts his top to inspect the wound, but feels a chill run up her spine.

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: You're armed...

steps.name: Babel Doctor
steps.text: Why didn't the guards check you...?
The light of the Soul Furnace lights up the night sky above Kazdel like the midday sun.
The fire's crackles echo like a mournful growl, a somber tribute to the fallen who have become its fuel.
All the Sarkaz set their eyes on the sky that night.
No one notices the light from one of the field hospital's windows go out.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Your Highness?

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Why was I brought here...? Oh, yes, I have good news to report...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What news?

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: We won.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: We defeated the Leithanians, Your Highness. Me, my son, and the Blue Blood Squad. We won, we won...

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Are you not glad, Your Highness? Were we too slow...?

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Blake! My son, bring me the battle plan! Son! Son?

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Sorry, Your Highness, I don't know where my son went...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You killed a doctor, one who has served Kazdel for years, treating Oripathy patients.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Kazdel? Doctor? No, you misunderstand, your Highness.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: I only fight Leithanians.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Have you read his emotions, Theresa?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Pain, confusion, madness. He has driven himself mad to escape the painful memories.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He doesn't even know what crime he committed.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The others do.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The guards discovered him brawling with another Sarkaz amid shattered casks of liquor, which ignited and spread fire throughout the field hospital.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All await the King's response. But you cannot be the one to do it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Leave it to me.

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Your Highness! General! I gave my all to defeat the Leithanians!

steps.name: Brooding Sarkaz
steps.text: Was I wrong to do so? Your Highness!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Take him away.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...His name is Logan, given to him by his mother, who was one of the first Babel engineers.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He hardly uses any Arts, but the guards were hypnotized by Arts. Someone is behind this.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Military Commission will not investigate the Sarkaz for the sake of an outsider, not after they've just been through another ordeal.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Neither should Babel.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We have no choice. The war has just ended.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Babel should withdraw from military and political affairs, at least for the time being.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You know that's not what Babel is about in the first place.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I do, but many don't.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I will define the parameters for Babel's activities. Babel members will continue to serve Kazdel's medical, educational, and technological needs from this area.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Military Commission will continue to protect them. But we must make every effort to avoid conflict.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: There will come a day when the repressed hatred boils over, and even we will be powerless when that day comes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel is in urgent need of a change. We have to solve the Originium problem... soon.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But even that won't solve all our problems.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I've always known.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: There you are, Ascalon.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What have you seen in this city?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Deth... People cry... People die.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Cry? Cry... tears?
Theresis stretches out his hand. A delicate stone knife lies in its palm.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Knife! My...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Keep it safe. A warrior should treasure her weapon.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I will teach you how to sharpen your blade.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But it's up to you to decide whom it cuts.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're too impatient, Theresis. She's not ready to understand these things yet.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: She has to understand, sooner or later.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Maybe. But for now, what we should do is give the frightened child a little bit of peace. Do you like this city, Ascalon?
Compared to the armored general, Ascalon does not like this Sarkaz woman crouched before her.
She seems to see through all of her thoughts, leaving no secrets—a most dangerous thing in the wastes.
But she cannot bring herself to be hostile to this gentle Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No need to be afraid. You know I don't mean you any harm. Come, touch my horn. We're the same.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Warm, here.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Warm, me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, warm. Hatred and killing are not the only way to solve a problem.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: (Slurring) Way? Probem?
Theresa says no more. It is difficult for a girl who has known nothing but the wastes to understand certain words, even with the help of the King of Sarkaz.
She takes Ascalon's hand.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's like the wound on your palm. Weapons can't heal it. Only time and medicine can.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Aw!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's okay. I've cleaned your wound. You'll need to take care of it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Be patient. One day, you'll wake up and find that it doesn't hurt anymore.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Yeah!
Babel Classroom, Kazdel

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...No one. Here.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We'll wait a little longer. It's not lesson time yet. They'll come—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Look, it's Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Casualty report from the Military Commission. There are many children, most of them students.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The ones that lived...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Their parents are no longer willing to let the outsiders of Babel teach them.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Plus, if memory serves, many of Babel's teachers have already left out of fear.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You're troubling yourself too much with trivial matters, Theresa. You need to rest. We still have to—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I want to wait a little longer, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...Very well.
He does not leave. The classroom is eerily quiet.
Theresa closes her eyes and recalls the students who used to fill the classroom.

a.text: 'They said we can get potatoes for coming to school!'
'I didn't understand that one, Your Highness. Do you have any simple stories?'
'You said you went to the outside with mercenaries when you were our age?'
'There's a sea between Sargon and Iberia? What's a boat? Why can't we go up on deck? Why would we throw up?'
'Leithanian spires? Are they like our furnace?'
'People who are nice to us? But Dad says there's no foreigners like that.'
'But the teachers here are nice to us!'

steps.text: Students come and go. But she always managed to get them to return.
But this time, no one came.

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: General Theresis! Your Highness! I—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You!
The hilt of a stone knife hits the boy in the chest. Although unable to break free, the boy strains to look up at the tall, gaunt girl who has him pinned.

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: I saw General Theresis come this way. I just wanted to—

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: Theresa, Your Highness! You're here, too! This classroom... are you teaching?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Put down the knife, Ascalon.

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: ...Your Highness!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You were looking for me?

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: Yes. I came to seek an answer for the children who lost their parents. I know the Military Commission will take care of them, as it took care of me...

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: But will this change anything? What if another war comes?

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: I want to change things, but I don't know what I can change, or what I should change.
The two rulers gaze upon the fearless child, each arriving at their own answer inside.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Brave Boy
steps.text: Manfred.

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: Dad, we've been standing at the door forever. Why can't we go in?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Mommy's hurt very badly. She needs some quiet to rest. We shouldn't bother her.

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: But I miss Mom...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Daddy misses her too, but not now... we'll go home together once I come back.

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: Where are you going, Dad?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I have to leave the city for a bit, to make the people who hurt Mommy pay.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Stay here with Mommy and wait for Daddy.

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: Can you stay, Daddy? We'll figure out a way to make Mommy better, I promise...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Do you like Mommy's name?

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: Odda... yes, it sounds very nice.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: It's your name now.

steps.name: Sleepy Child
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I'll teach you to fight the bad guys with Mommy's weapon once I get back.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Okay! I'll beat up the bad guys who hurt Mommy!

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: But will beating up the bad guys make her feel better?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: You'll understand someday... Odda.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: ...I'll be back. Wait for me.
Goodluck turns around, toward the crystal-infested city wall.
The only thing left that ties him to this city is Odda.
Odda... and Odda.
